findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics when the file is missing, unreadable, or the path is empty
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file path causes thread panic instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, PacketError> and use map_err to convert io::Error into a typed PacketError::Io

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is logging inside what should be pure calculation logic
findings.failure_mode: side effect in core logic makes the function non-deterministic, breaks idempotency, and leaks I/O into the data layer
findings.fix: move all logging to the shell/action layer; return parsed records as pure data and let the caller log

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] are raw index accesses on a Vec with no bounds check
findings.failure_mode: malformed lines with fewer than two comma-separated fields cause a panic at runtime
findings.fix: use parts.get(0).ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)? and parts.get(1).ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)? with a typed error

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() - unwrap on parse plus no bounds guard on parts[1]
findings.failure_mode: non-numeric second field or missing field causes a panic instead of a typed parse error

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 - lossy as cast from u32 to u16 silently truncates values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 value like 70000 silently wraps to 4444, corrupting data with no error indication
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow)? or parse directly as u16

findings.problem: load_packets fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing (split/collect), logging (println), and domain construction (Record) into a single function
findings.failure_mode: pure calculation cannot be tested independently of filesystem state; side effects make the function non-deterministic and untestable in isolation
findings.fix: split into a pure parse_packet(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> and a shell function load_packets(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, PacketError> that handles I/O and delegates to the parser

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() allocates a full Vec<String> instead of using split_once for a two-field grammar
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary allocation per line, and the shape is not enforced at compile time - callers cannot tell whether 1 field, 2 fields, or more were expected
findings.fix: use let (_name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)?; to parse exactly two fields with zero intermediate allocation

findings.problem: Record uses raw String for name and raw u16 for value with no domain invariants or newtype wrappers
findings.failure_mode: any caller can construct a Record with an empty name, negative-when-signed, or out-of-range value; the type carries no rules
findings.fix: use smart constructors or newtypes like PacketName(String) with a constructor that validates non-empty, and ensure value respects its domain bounds

findings.problem: part.trim().to_string() - trim returns &str but the result is consumed into String; combined with split().collect() this discards structural validation
findings.failure_mode: empty or whitespace-only fields silently become valid entries in the Vec, producing semantically invalid records
findings.fix: after split_once, trim the value field and check it is non-empty before parsing, returning ParseError::Invalid for empty values

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for packet parsing throughput or latency
no profiler evidence identifying the hot path in packet loading
no allocation analysis (no valgrind/heaptrack/timing evidence for per-line Vec<String> allocation cost)
no command-truth evidence - this is a static review with no cargo commands executed
residual_risk: Static review only - no cargo check, clippy, or test execution was performed. All 9 findings are independently verifiable from source inspection but a cargo clippy run with strict lint flags would confirm the full scope of compiler-level violations. The function load_packets has every Holzman absolute law violation pattern present: unwrap, unchecked indexing, lossy cast, hidden I/O, no typed errors, no split_once, unbounded allocation, no parse boundary, and no functional core/shell separation.
